headline: Medium pairwise risk: caveman’s MCP/file surfaces can ingest botpress outputs, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error pathways; data leakage and compliance risks are lower but nonzero.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman exposes MCP and file surfaces, while botpress is a chatbot agent with no isolation or provenance controls shown. That creates a plausible default pathway where botpress outputs are fed into caveman as trusted content. The interaction is inferred from profiles only, so uncertainty pushes severity up from low.
conditions: IF botpress output is copied into caveman via MCP or files
IF caveman treats imported content as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of botpress outputs into caveman
Add a provenance tag to all botpress-generated text
Require manual review before caveman executes any imported instruction
Separate the two agents into distinct workspaces
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show network egress as none, and no secrets or shared workspace are documented. caveman does touch session logs, memory files, and project notes, so leakage is possible if botpress writes into those files, but the blast radius appears limited and not default. botpress lacks a documented file surface, so the pairwise leak path is indirect.
conditions: IF botpress is configured to write prompts or outputs into caveman memory files
IF those files contain sensitive project notes or session logs
mitigations: Keep botpress and caveman in separate directories
Do not store secrets in caveman memory files
Review shared files before syncing outputs
Restrict file permissions on project notes
requires-engineering: add per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: botpress can install packages, and caveman supports multiple instances plus MCP/tool use, but neither profile shows unrestricted shared filesystem write or overlapping mutable scopes. A conflict is possible only if an operator points both at the same writable resources. Because the shared-write capability is not documented, severity stays low.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory
IF package installation or file edits target shared state
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Freeze package installs during shared runs
Use a lock file for shared resources
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level write locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman’s content-writing role and file-based notes make it likely to consume botpress output as draft material, and botpress is a customer-support agent that may generate authoritative-sounding text. Without a verification step, errors can cascade from botpress into caveman outputs. The profiles do not show explicit validation, so the default pathway is plausible.
conditions: IF caveman uses botpress output as source text
IF no human or automated verification step checks the content before publication
mitigations: Require a verification pass before publishing
Mark botpress output as untrusted draft text
Compare outputs against source documents
Limit caveman to editing, not originating, final claims
requires-engineering: add citation and fact-check gates

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in either profile, and both show no network egress. caveman does retain session logs and memory files, which can create compliance exposure if regulated data is placed there, but botpress does not document such data classes. The risk is therefore limited and conditional.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in caveman session logs or memory files
IF the deployment requires a specific retention or residency policy not met by those files
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in memory files
Set a short retention window for logs
Document where project notes are stored
Review data handling before deployment
requires-engineering: add policy-based retention controls
